segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Good morning and welcome to the University of Westlands.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: My name is Marcia Mayhew and I’m the co-ordinator of the Bachelor of Social Science degree.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: This morning I’d like to tell you about the structure of the university and about some of the requirements of the degree that you’re about to enter.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: The Bachelor of Social Science is in one faculty within the university, that is the faculty where I work, known as Arts and Social Sciences.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Here on this campus we also have the faculties of Architecture, Law and Science and Technology among others.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: It’s important to know something about the structure of the faculty because, as you go through your course, you may need to call on members of the staff to help you.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: At the top of the faculty we have a dean and below the dean we have three divisions; each division has a divisional head and your degree is located in the Division of Social Sciences.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Within each of the divisions, there are the departments and each of these offers the different degrees.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: For instance two of the departments which offer the major subjects for your award are Sociology and Psychology.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Each has a departmental head but for practical purposes the people you are going to see the most of are myself as co-ordinator of the social sciences degree and the actual lecturers who are teaching the subjects that you are taking.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: For instance in the first semester you’ll be doing four subjects psychology sociology history and economics.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: If you have any problems or difficulties, not that I’m anticipating you will, but you never know, then you should go and see your lecturers.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: For instance, you may find that you can’t meet a deadline for an essay or perhaps you’re having problems with attendance.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: These seem to be the two most common problems that students face.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: If your lecturers are unavailable, you can always come and see me in my office.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: I’m available on Wednesday and Thursday mornings and on Friday afternoons. Outside these hours, perhaps you could ring the secretary and make an appointment.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Now you’ll note that all of the subjects which you undertake in the first year are composed of lectures and tutorials.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: A lecture is about an hour long and a tutorial usually runs for about two hours.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: A lecture is rather like what I am doing now where one person will talk to all of you together on a subject.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: We do ask you to try to attend the lectures.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: A tutorial is perhaps where most of the learning occurs at a university.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: You will be divided into groups of between 12 and 15 students and each week one of you will have to present a piece of work to the group as a whole and then the group will discuss what you’ve said.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: It’s this discussion, this exchange of ideas, which really constitutes the basis of university learning, in my view.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Listening to lectures in many ways is just giving you information that you could access for yourself in the library but the discussion at the tutorial is very important.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: This doesn’t mean that you shouldn’t go to the lectures though!

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Other factors to be particularly concerned about are the structure of essays and delivery of written material and in particular I would like to mention the question of plagiarism.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Plagiarism is taking other people’s work without acknowledging it, that is, without saying where it comes from.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Of course all essays are based on research done by other people but you must remember to attribute the work to the original writer.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: And while it’s a good idea to work with other people don’t hand in work which is exactly the same as your friend’s work because we will notice!

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: If you don’t acknowledge the source of your information then you run the risk of failing the subject or in very serious cases you might be denied entry to the university.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Last but not least, stay in touch with us.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: If things are getting you down, don’t go and hide.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Come and talk to us about it.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: That’s what we are here for.

segments.speaker: LECTURER
segments.en: Right, thank you very much for coming along today.
